chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Musadif, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman who performs Hajj on behalf of the man who has not performed it (Saroura), he said: 'If she had already performed Hajj, and she was a Muslim, an understanding one (faqeehah); for there are women who are more understanding than men.'

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةِ: A person who has not yet performed their obligatory Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a woman to perform Hajj on behalf of a man who hasn't performed it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a woman may perform Hajj on behalf of a man, provided she is Muslim and possesses sufficient religious understanding (faqeehah), emphasizing that gender does not preclude spiritual or intellectual superiority. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on individual piety and knowledge over gender in the validity of religious duties, reflecting the broader principle that 'faqah' (deep understanding) is the true measure of religious competence.
